Getting Started with Macros

Everything you need to know to start using SolidWorks macros at Nordic Minesteel. Whether you're brand new or just need a refresher.

🤔 What is a macro?

A macro is a small program that runs inside SolidWorks. Instead of manually clicking through menus, typing in property values, creating PDFs, or repeating the same 20 steps for every file — you press one button and the macro does it all instantly.

Every macro on this site was built specifically for Nordic Minesteel's workflow. They know our PDM vault, our folder structures, our property names, our templates, and our manufacturing limits. They're not generic tools — they're custom-built for how we work.

⚡ The #1 rule: Check out your files first

If the file isn't checked out, Prepare for CADLink silently skips it. No error, no warning — it just does nothing to that model.

Before running Prepare for CADLink, check the model out in PDM. If you don't, the macro will see the read-only file, log "Model is not checked out by us — will skip", and move on without writing any properties.

Other macros behave differently — for example PDMPDF1 attempts to check out the model itself when generating PDFs. When in doubt, check out first.

Remember: Checked out = changes save. Checked in = Prepare for CADLink skips the file. Check the lock icon in PDM before running.

▶️ How to run a macro

All macros are run from a toolbar button in SolidWorks — one click and go. If you don't have the buttons yet, ask Dylan. Takes about a minute to add all the macros you need.

Don't try to run macros from Tools → Macro → Run — that path can't pass the settings the macros need, so things won't work right. Always use a toolbar button.

Adding a button yourself (optional — easier to just ask Dylan):

1

Right-click any toolbar in SolidWorks and choose Customize…

2

Go to the Commands tab and find the Macros category.

3

Drag the New Macro Button onto any toolbar.

4

Browse to the macro file (.swp), pick an icon, give it a name, click OK.

5

Done — one click to run from now on.

📋 Which macro do I need?

I need to get a model ready for CADLink
Prepare for CADLink — the main one. Check out the model, run it, fill in anything it flags as red (Revision, Product Group), done. Works on single parts or entire assemblies.
I need to create PDFs from drawings
PDMPDF1 — run it from a single drawing, an assembly (creates PDFs for everything), or batch-process a whole folder. Also has an audit mode to check what's missing.
I need to create a DXF burn profile
PDMDXF — select the flat face you want to cut, run the macro. Be careful to pick the right face (watch out for counter-sinks).
I need to clean up properties for PDM
MoveToPDM — talk to Dylan first. The rules need to be configured for your specific batch of files. It's powerful but needs setup.
I need to convert metric models to imperial
ModelToImperial — open the part or assembly, run it. Converts everything including sub-parts automatically.

⚠️ Troubleshooting

The macro runs but nothing seems to happen
Make sure the right type of file is open — each macro needs a specific type (part, assembly, or drawing). Check the macro's page in this guide for what it expects. Also make sure the file is checked out.
Properties filled in but disappeared after closing
The file wasn't checked out. Check it out in PDM, run the macro again, and the changes will stick this time.
SolidWorks shows a security warning
Click "Enable macros" — all macros here are written in-house by Dylan and are safe to run.
The macro gave an unexpected result
Use Ctrl+Z (undo) — most changes can be undone. Then submit a bug report in the Requests tab so Dylan can investigate.
A macro is missing or broken
The file may have been updated or moved. Contact Dylan directly — he can fix it in minutes.
Can I break something by running a macro?
Generally no — PDM keeps full version history so nothing is ever truly lost. But for batch operations (processing hundreds of files), always check with Dylan first if you're not sure about the settings.

Crash Donut Duty — Official Terms, Conditions & Ceremonial Acceptance Record

By logging a crash you are executing the office's most serious non-legal donut pact. Read the full terms below — the "Agree and play" button stays locked until you scroll all the way to the bottom.

Article 1 — Preamble

Welcome to Crash Donut Duty ("the Game"), a voluntary, morale-boosting monthly competition operated inside Nordic Minesteel by the Macro Guide. The Game exists to turn the shared experience of SolidWorks unexpectedly closing into something lighter for the team, while keeping the monthly donut duty clear and visible. By clicking "Agree and play" below, you ("the Player" or "you") enter into a ceremonial, non-legal, office-social agreement with every other Player ("the League"), the Macro Guide ("the Platform"), and the Commissioner of Donut Duty ("Dylan Lebel"). This document supersedes any previous agreement, verbal handshake, donut promise, snack-side letter, or scratch-pad scoring scheme.

Article 2 — Eligibility & Enrollment

The Game is open to any Nordic Minesteel team member who regularly uses SolidWorks and wants to join a light office competition. Enrollment is performed by clicking "Agree and play." The act of clicking constitutes your electronic acknowledgement, ceremonial signature, and office-game acceptance of these Terms in their entirety. The scroll requirement and minimum review timer exist so everyone has a fair chance to review the rules before joining.

Article 3 — What Counts as a Crash

A "Crash" means any unscheduled, involuntary, software-induced cessation of SolidWorks functionality that interrupts your work. This includes hard freezes, the "SolidWorks has stopped responding" dialog, the quiet close that loses unsaved work, and the full-PC reboot. Severity does not matter for scoring. A minor "ugh, save again" counts the same as a catastrophic "I'm rebuilding the assembly from a backup" event. The League decided this in the interest of speed; questions can be raised with the Commissioner.

Article 4 — What Does Not Count

The following are not crashes for the purposes of the Game and must not be logged: (i) you closed SolidWorks on purpose; (ii) you got the spinning wheel for ten seconds and then it came back; (iii) PDM threw an error but SolidWorks itself kept running; (iv) Windows Update rebooted your machine; (v) someone tripped over your power cable; (vi) you opened a 4 GB assembly with the visualization graph wide open and SolidWorks did the only sensible thing. Logging non-crashes is a violation of Article 9 (Honor System) and may result in a stern look from Dylan Lebel.

Article 5 — Scoring & Standings

Each valid Crash logged contributes one (1) point to the Player's monthly tally. Standings are visible in real time on the Leaderboard. The Player with the highest tally at the moment the month closes is declared the Monthly Champion and receives Donut Duty for the next month. Ties are governed by Article 8.

Article 6 — Monthly Cycle & Lock-In

The competition runs from the first calendar day of the month at 12:00 AM local time through the last calendar day of the month at 4:30 PM local time, at which point the Leaderboard is permanently locked for that month. Crashes logged after the lock-in time roll forward into the following month's standings. Each month is independent; there is no carry-over, no grand total, no season points, and no playoff bracket. Past months remain visible because gloating is, in the considered opinion of the Commissioner, a load-bearing element of office culture.

Article 7 — Donut Duty (The Prize That Is Also a Punishment)

The Monthly Champion shall, no later than the end of the first full work week of the following month, supply the office with a quantity of donuts equal to at least one (1) normal full-size donut per active Player, including the Champion themselves. "Active Player" means any Player who logged at least one crash in the closing month. Acceptable donuts include glazed, chocolate-glazed, maple, Boston cream, jelly, sprinkle, and old-fashioned. Munchkins, Timbits, and donut holes are not acceptable substitutes and shall be considered an attempt to defraud the League. Gluten-free or vegan options are encouraged in addition to, not in place of, traditional donuts where any Player has dietary restrictions.

Article 8 — Tie-Break

In the event two or more Players are tied for first place at lock-in, the tie shall be resolved by the most recent applicable team poll. The current resolution method (as of the version of these Terms you are reading) is "one week each": each tied Champion serves a separate week of Donut Duty in the following month. The Commissioner reserves the right to put alternate methods (wheel-spin, snack-split, etc.) to a vote at any time.

Article 9 — Honor System

This is office fun, not a sworn legal proceeding. Players agree to log only real SolidWorks crashes that genuinely happened, in real time, on their actual workstation. The Platform does not, will not, and frankly cannot verify a crash automatically. The integrity of the Game depends entirely on everyone playing it straight. Suspected discrepancies may be brought to the attention of the Commissioner, who may, at his sole discretion, void crashes, correct standings, or update these Terms to close the gap. Disputes are handled privately, not on the leaderboard.

Article 10 — Voluntary Participation & Spectator Mode

Participation in the Game is and shall remain entirely voluntary. A Player who does not wish to participate in a given month may click "Decline (spectator only)" below. Doing so will: (a) lock that Player out of logging crashes for the remainder of the calendar month; (b) preserve any crashes already logged but exclude the Player from prize calculations for that month; (c) save an opt-out snapshot of the Player's current-month crash records; and (d) reduce the Player's status, for that month, to "Spectator," with full read access to the Leaderboard and zero donut obligation. A Spectator may, at any time during the month, return to active play by clicking "Join now" — they will then be subject to all Articles of these Terms as if they had never declined, including Article 7 if they should crash their way to the top.

Article 11 — Notifications

Players may opt in or out of crash notifications independently of their playing status. Receipt of a notification does not create any additional obligation to bring donuts, react immediately, or comment on someone else's crash.

Article 12 — Privacy

The Game records, for each Crash, the Player who logged it, the chosen severity level, the timestamp, and the Windows account that submitted the entry. It also records each Player's current Terms acceptance status, acceptance timestamp, display name, Windows username, and rules version so the team can see who is participating under the current version and review the ceremonial signature record. This data is stored locally on the Y: drive in plain JSON and is visible to anyone with access to the Macro Guide. The Game does not record the contents of your model, the cause of the crash, or anything else from your workstation.

Article 13 — Commissioner's Authority

Dylan Lebel ("the Commissioner") reserves the unilateral right to modify, amend, suspend, replace, retire, reinstate, or completely rewrite these Terms at any point, for any reason or for no reason, with or without notice, with or without explanation, and with or without your continued blessing. Such changes may be applied retroactively to the current month if, in the Commissioner's sole judgment, the change is necessary to preserve the spirit of the Game, prevent a loophole, accommodate an act of God, accommodate a sudden donut shortage, or simply because it sounded funnier that way. When these Terms change, every Player will be required to re-accept the new version before logging any further crashes. Players who disagree with a change may decline that month and remain in Spectator Mode; they may not, however, retroactively unaccept previously logged crashes or escape Donut Duty already earned.

Article 14 — No Warranty

The Game, the Leaderboard, the Macro Guide, and any donuts produced as a consequence of the foregoing are provided "as is" and "as crashed." The Commissioner makes no representation as to the freshness, flavor, fillability, or icing-to-cake ratio of any donut delivered in fulfillment of Article 7. Players are encouraged to consider dietary preferences and enjoy responsibly.

Article 15 — Limitation of Liability

To the maximum extent permitted by office norms and basic decency, the Commissioner, the Platform, the League, and any individual Player shall not be liable for: lost work caused by SolidWorks crashes; disappointment with the monthly standings; snack-related inconvenience; or any other consequential, incidental, or punitive damages arising from your participation in the Game. Your available remedy in the event of dissatisfaction is to decline participation for the month or raise a question with the Commissioner.

Article 16 — Severability

If any provision of these Terms is found by competent authority (defined as: the Commissioner; failing which, a coin-flip) to be unenforceable or overly silly, that provision shall be struck and the remainder of the Terms shall continue in full force and effect.

Article 17 — Entire Agreement

These Terms constitute the entire agreement between you and the League with respect to Crash Donut Duty and supersede any prior verbal agreement, slack message, hallway promise, or scribbled whiteboard scoring system. There are no oral side-letters, no secret bonus categories, and no exempt status for senior staff.

Article 18 — Acceptance

By clicking "Agree and play," you confirm: (i) you have read these Terms in their entirety, or at least scrolled past every word of them with sincere intent to read; (ii) you understand and accept Article 7; (iii) you acknowledge that the Commissioner can, per Article 13, change the rules at any time, and you accept this in advance; (iv) you adopt your display name and Windows username as your ceremonial electronic signature for Game records; (v) you are mentally prepared to bring donuts; and (vi) you understand that nothing here is legally binding but everything here is socially binding, which in a workplace is the binding that actually matters.

Article 19 — Signed Terms Record

Upon acceptance, the Platform shall create and retain a ceremonial acceptance record showing the Player's display name, Windows username, acceptance timestamp, and accepted rules version. The League may inspect accepted Players' signed Terms from the Participants & terms panel. Such inspection is intended for transparency, jokes, snack accountability, and gentle prevention of "I never agreed to this" arguments.

Article 20 — Ceremonial Non-Legal Status

For the avoidance of doubt, and with maximum fake solemnity, these Terms are drafted to resemble an Extremely Serious Agreement while remaining an office game document only. Nothing herein creates an employment contract, payroll deduction authorization, purchase order, legal claim, court-enforceable obligation, or actual attorney-client anything. The intended enforcement mechanisms are leaderboard visibility, peer accountability, and the ancient power of remembering who promised donuts.

— End of Terms & Conditions, version . Scroll up if you need to re-read any of it. The "Agree and play" button is now armed below.
